title: Half of Americans Use Chatbots — Most Think AI Is Moving Too Fast
hook: A new Pew poll captures the mood of the AI era: chatbot use has jumped to about half of Americans, yet nearly two-thirds say the technology is advancing too quickly.
key_points: Pew found 49% of Americans use AI chatbots at least occasionally — up from 33% in 2024.
About 44% report using ChatGPT specifically — roughly double its 2023 level.
Yet 63% think AI is advancing too quickly for comfort.
Rapid adoption and widespread unease are happening at the same time.
content_html: If you've started using AI chatbots but feel a little uneasy about how fast it's all moving, you're in good company. A new Pew Research poll, reported by The Verge, finds that about 49 percent of Americans now use AI chatbots at least occasionally — up sharply from roughly 33 percent in 2024 — with around 44 percent using ChatGPT specifically, roughly double its 2023 level.
extra_html: The twist is how people feel about it: some 63 percent say AI is advancing too quickly. So the picture isn't "people love it" or "people reject it" — it's both at once. Adoption is climbing fast even as a clear majority wishes the technology would slow down. That mix of curiosity and caution is arguably the healthiest stance there is: useful enough to reach for, new enough to keep your guard up. If you're just dipping in, you're not behind — and you're not alone in wanting to take it carefully.
